properties.decision:
reflow2 will not evaluate whether what you asked for is a good idea, whether your logic holds, or whether your requirement will produce the outcome you want. It records intent faithfully and threads it rigorously. A design can be perfectly coherent and completely wrong, and reflow2 will report it as coherent — correctly.

WHOSE JOB IT IS: a person who understands the domain. Reflow2's own doctrine already says so — `dec:three-party-checks`: "the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides."

⚠️ WHY IT IS WRITTEN DOWN. Anthony named it as the deepest of the AI-agent pitfalls on 2026-08-17: "if your initial prompt contains a logical flaw, the agent will perfectly implement your flawed logic instead of questioning it." A DESIGN GRAPH DOES NOT FIX THAT — it makes the flawed logic durable, traceable and consistently applied, which is arguably worse than leaving it in a chat log, because now it has authority. Recording intent well and recording intent CORRECTLY are different acts, and reflow2 only does the first.

⇒ WHAT REFLOW2 DOES DO NEARBY, and it is a real fraction of the problem rather than a consolation: it catches DISAGREEMENT WITH YOURSELF. A `CONTRADICTS` edge and the `contradiction` detector surface a new claim that conflicts with a settled one; `kpp_contradicted` does it for inviolable intent; `detect_gaps` puts the questions it cannot answer back to you rather than guessing. So when a flawed instruction contradicts something you already decided, reflow2 will say so. When the flaw is consistent with everything else you have said, nothing in the graph can see it.

📌 THE HONEST FRAMING FOR A USER: reflow2 raises the cost of being INCONSISTENT and does nothing to the cost of being WRONG. That asymmetry is worth knowing before relying on it.

RECORDED AS A NON-GOAL, 2026-08-17. Retiring it is part of shipping anything that voids it — though of the four, this is the one least likely ever to be voided.
properties.name: NON-GOAL — reflow2 does not tell you your requirement is WRONG; it can only tell you it disagrees with something you already settled
properties.rationale: A design graph does not fix a flawed premise; it makes the flaw durable, traceable and consistently applied, which is arguably worse than a chat log because it now carries authority. What reflow2 can genuinely catch is disagreement with something already settled, via CONTRADICTS and the contradiction detector. It raises the cost of being inconsistent and does nothing to the cost of being wrong — an asymmetry worth stating before anyone relies on it.
